Oh See Threee Lite

Audio-Source-Oscillator Single-Voice Analog Pitch Synth

Oh See Threee Lite gives you the hands-on controls of an analog synth, with your incoming audio as the sound source. Its octave paths draw on the dividers and rectifiers of vintage analog octave circuitry. Choose one of five positions (−2, −1, 0, +1, or +2 octaves) and use the independent Dry Blend to mix in the original sound.

Set the selected voice’s pan, delay, and filter from the front panel. Add movement with the LFO, envelope follower, or noise source.

Quick start

  1. Insert Oh See Threee Lite on a stereo audio track or bus in a host that supports stereo VST3 effects. Feed audio through the track to drive the octave paths.
  2. Select −2, −1, 0, +1, or +2 in Octave Voice. Only one position plays at a time. 0 is unshifted.
  3. For octave positions, watch Open while adjusting Gate, Hysteresis, Sub Range, and Detector Gain. The 0 position and independent Dry Blend stay audible when the gate closes.
  4. Set Voice Level, Pan, and Delay. Adjust the octave voice filter and Up Edge, then raise Dry Level from its default −60 dB if you want more direct input.
  5. Watch the stereo Output meters as you set Output. The On / Off rocker passes the original input at its original level when switched to Off.

Drag a knob or fader to adjust it. Its value appears in a small bubble while you move the control. Click INFO in the header to open the About panel. Drag the bottom-right resize grip to resize the editor proportionally.

Controls

Tracking

Printed control Range Default Use
Gate −60 to 0 dB −40 dB Mutes generated octave voices below the threshold. The unshifted 0 position and Dry Blend stay audible.
Hysteresis 0–100% 50% Sets how far the detector signal must swing before a new cycle counts. Very low values can retrigger on bright input. Very high values can miss soft notes.
Sub Range 50–600 Hz 300 Hz Low-pass cutoff for the signal used to generate the lower octave positions. Lower values reduce brighter content in those voices.
Detector Gain 1–10× 2× Drives the pitch-detector signal and leaves voice output level unchanged. Raise it if tracking does not lock onto weak or complex input.

The Open lamp lights while the gate is open and the octave voices can pass.

Octave Voice and Dry Blend

Choose one octave button at a time. −2 is two octaves down, −1 is one octave down, 0 is unshifted, and +1 or +2 is one or two octaves up. The selected path has its own level, pan, delay, and filter. The separate Dry Blend remains available for every selection.

The unshifted 0 position stays audible when the octave Gate closes. It still follows the selected voice's level, pan, delay, filter, and modulation controls.

Area / printed control Range or choices Default Use
−2, −1, 0, +1, +2 Five positions 0 Selects the single voice position.
Voice Level −60 to +12 dB 0 dB Sets the selected voice level. Its fader meter shows activity in that voice.
Pan L 100 to C to R 100 C Places the selected voice in the stereo field. The value bubble shows C, L n, or R n.
Delay 0–50 ms 0 ms Offsets the selected voice in time. The control sets an audio-path delay in milliseconds.
Up Edge 0–100% 70% Shapes the edge of the +1 and +2 rectifier paths. Higher settings make the edge harder and more fuzzy. Lower settings sound smoother.
Octave Freq 80–12,000 Hz 12,000 Hz Low-pass cutoff for the selected voice.
Octave Res Q 0.50–8.00 Q 0.71 Resonance of the octave voice low-pass filter.
Octave Voice On rocker On / off On The rocker engages the low-pass when up. Down bypasses it. The filter follows the selected voice's delay.
Dry Level −60 to +12 dB −60 dB Sets the independent clean input blend. Raise it to add the unprocessed input under the selected voice. Its fader meter shows Dry Blend activity.
Dry Pan L 100 to C to R 100 C Places Dry Blend in the stereo field.
Dry Freq 80–12,000 Hz 12,000 Hz Low-pass cutoff for Dry Blend.
Dry Res Q 0.50–8.00 Q 0.71 Resonance of the Dry Blend low-pass filter.
Dry Blend On rocker On / off On The rocker engages the Dry Blend low-pass when up. Down bypasses it.

Dry Blend is a separate clean tap of the input. Its own level, pan, and optional low-pass filter shape a path that bypasses the gate, modulation, and delay.

Modulation

The three glass displays show LFO, ENV, and Noise. Each source has Dly, Pan, and Flt depth faders. Set a depth to 0% to disable that connection. Positive and negative values move the selected voice in opposite directions.

Printed control Range or choices Default Use
Wave Sine, Triangle, Saw Up, Saw Down, Square, Random Sine Chooses the LFO shape.
Rate 0.05–20 Hz 0.50 Hz Sets the LFO speed in cycles per second.
Attack 1–250 ms 15 ms Sets the envelope follower's attack.
Release 5–1,000 ms 15 ms Sets how quickly the envelope follower falls after input level drops.
Texture 0–100% 35% Low settings smooth the Noise source. Higher settings make it faster and more jittery.
Dly, Pan, Flt Each −100% to +100% 0% Set each source's depth to voice delay, stereo pan, or the octave voice filter cutoff. Delay modulation can create pitch movement.

The Dry Blend path stays outside this modulation. Its pan and filter remain steady.

Starting points

Try these as first settings with a source you know:

  • Sub voice: Select −1 or −2 and set Voice Level to taste. Keep Dry Level near its −60 dB starting point to hear the octave voice clearly.
  • Upper voice: Select +1 or +2. Adjust Up Edge to shape the rectifier edge, then set Voice Level for the source.
  • Unison with dry: Select 0, then raise Dry Level to mix the direct input with the processed unshifted voice. Adjust their two Pan controls independently.

Divider

Printed control Choices Default Use
Sub Mode Polarity / Magnitude Magnitude Chooses how the lower octave is formed. Polarity flips the waveform on divider cycles. Magnitude rectifies and reapplies level.
Sub2 Mode Cascade /4 / Re-detect Cascade /4 Chooses how the −2 position is made. Cascade divides again. Re-detect follows the −1 path again.

Master and bypass

Printed control or display Range Default Use
Output −60 to +12 dB 0 dB Sets the final level after the selected voice and Dry Blend are combined.
Stereo Output meters Left and right −72 dB when silent Show the stereo output peaks.
On / Off rocker On / Off On Set it to Off to pass the stereo input through at its original level. A host may also provide its own plug-in bypass.

Presets and sessions

Lite has no built-in factory preset list or preset-saving display. Save the plug-in state with your DAW project or use any preset feature supplied by your host.

Installation and limits

The configured release workflow targets Windows x64 VST3 and Linux x86_64 VST3. Check your download for the packages it includes. The source declares a Standalone format. The release workflow packages VST3. No macOS, Audio Units (AU), or AAX target is configured, so the configured formats do not provide an AU build for Logic or an AAX build for Pro Tools. This manual does not list DAW-version compatibility. Use a host that supports stereo VST3 audio effects.

For a VST3 ZIP installation, close your DAW and copy the Sunbunny Oh See Threee Lite.vst3 bundle into the VST3 folder for your system. Reopen the host and rescan its plug-ins.

  • Windows: C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3\
  • Linux: ~/.vst3/ (create the folder if needed, and use this only for a Linux package supplied with your download)

To remove a ZIP installation, close your DAW and delete only the Sunbunny Oh See Threee Lite.vst3 bundle from the folder where you installed it.

Windows builds may require the latest supported Microsoft Visual C++ v14 Redistributable (x64). If the host reports a missing MSVCP140.dll or VCRUNTIME140.dll, install Microsoft's supported x64 runtime from its current redistributable information or x64 installer.

Lite accepts stereo audio input and produces stereo audio output. MIDI input and output are disabled. Delay reaches 50 ms, and modulation can move the selected voice's delay time. The processor reports zero tail duration to the host, so leave extra time after the final note in exports and inspect the rendered ending. Consult any third-party notices supplied with your download for license information about bundled components.

For a product question, visit GitHub Discussions. For a bug, open GitHub Issues and include the plug-in version, operating system, host and version, sample rate, buffer size, the controls involved, and steps to reproduce the problem. Remove private audio or project material before attaching anything.

About

Hello! I’m Phillip Adkins, the musician and developer behind Sunbunny. I’ve been writing code and developing audio and machine learning algorithms for 15+ years.

I’m heavily jazz influenced, love classical impressionism, and have an unhealthily large collection of weird effects pedals I’m constantly tweaking. You’ll hear that mix in my guitar-centric instrumental music and in the plug-ins I make, including Oh See Threee.
